action: If you use Divalto-hosted services, ask Divalto for its incident status and confirm whether your data was affected; expect delays from BLDD and Pollen and confirm book orders another way where needed.
date_note: BLDD says the attack began on 15 November; ActuaLitté reports access problems from 13 November and Livres Hebdo gives Saturday 15 November, a mismatch with the calendar.
exec: A software supplier shut its platform for all customers, which stopped order handling at book distributors for about two days; one provider's outage can halt many firms.
impact: More than 1,000 Divalto customers had access cut; distributors BLDD (about 200 publishers) and Pollen could not work for about two days.
plain: A French business-software company was hit by a cyberattack and cut off all its customers as a precaution. Book distributors that rely on it were disrupted for about two days.

key_findings: BLDD told clients that Divalto has faced a targeted cyberattack since 15 November.
Divalto isolated its platform and closed access for all customers, reported by Livres Hebdo as more than 1,000 companies.
BLDD regained access on the morning of 17 November; Pollen says it could not work for two days and was back to normal on 17 November.
No attacker, data theft or ransom is reported.

summary: Divalto, a French business-software company based near Strasbourg, reported a security incident on its SaaS platform and shut customer access as a precaution. Book distributors BLDD and Pollen lost their order software for about two days; BLDD regained access on 17 November. Reports name no attacker and no data theft.
title: Divalto cyberattack cuts customer access, disrupting French book distributors

validation.note: ActuaLitté (citing BLDD and Pollen), Livres Hebdo and Cyberattaque.org agree on the incident and the platform shutdown; Divalto's own statement was not read, and the start date differs between outlets.

review.note: SaaS incident, precautionary access cut, BLDD/Pollen two-day outage, BLDD restored Nov 17 match ActuaLitté, Livres Hebdo, Cyberattaque.org; start-date conflict noted
